question: Who was credited with discovering the hydrogen isotope, or heavy hydrogen, for which he later received the 1934 Nobel Prize in Chemistry?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Harold C Urey**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Swedish chemist, engineer, and industrialist Alfred Nobel, through his will, established the five Nobel prizes in 1895.
 
• The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in the year 1901.
 
• The Nobel Prize is a set of awards that are given annually in recognition of scientific, academic, and cultural achievements in 6 categories Physics, Chemistry, Medicine or Physiology, Economics, Peace, and Literature.
